medicaid.what_the_table_says: The governing document is the Medi-Cal Part 2 provider manual section 'Non-Specialty Mental Health Services: Reimbursement Rates and Billing Codes' (file 'nonspecmentalcd.pdf'), retrieved live from two independent asset paths on mcweb.apps.prd.cammis.medi-cal.ca.gov and byte-identical (md5 c42bbfa94b91cc2e72be01364d2e6112). It genuinely has two provider-type columns, headed exactly 'MD, NP, PA' and 'LP, LCSW, LPCC, LMFT'. The preamble states: 'The rate at which a NSMHS may be reimbursed is dependent on whether the service is administered by a medical doctor (MD), nurse practitioner (NP), physician assistant (PA), Licensed Psychologist (LP), Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor (LPCC), Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) and/or a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT).' Rates are maximum allowances under 22 CCR 51505.3. The Psychotherapy Code Table is stamped 'Page updated: December 2022' (the Psychiatric Diagnostic Evaluation table likewise; the Miscellaneous NSMHS table was updated March 2025, confirming the document is live and maintained). The claim holds: $98.02 is the MD/NP/PA column, and the LMFT/LCSW/LPCC/psychologist column pays $38.01 for 90837. The page's 'Medi-Cal, 2026 (90837) = $98' row is therefore the physician column, and the '2026' date stamp is also wrong for this table.

medicaid.ninety_837_pays_less_than_90834: Confirmed, verbatim from the table. In the licensed column 90837 (60 min) pays $38.01 while 90834 (45 min) pays $67.16 — the longer code pays 43.4% less. This is what the published schedule says. It also looks internally anomalous rather than intentional: $38.01 is the exact value published one row down for 90839 (crisis, first 60 minutes) in BOTH columns, and $18.98 — the licensed-column value for 90832 — is the exact value published for 90840 and for 99366/99368 in the Case Management table. The pattern is consistent with a column/row transcription defect in the DHCS document. No DHCS erratum or correcting provider bulletin was found. Recommendation: report it as 'what the published schedule says', flag the anomaly, and do not present $38.01 as a settled economic fact about a 60-minute session.
medicaid.associate_finding: The current page's claim that an associate is paid the same $98 is wrong, and there is no associate rate at all. The same manual section, under 'Supervising Clinician Billing Requirements for Psychological Services', states: 'Associate marriage and family therapists, associate professional clinical counselors, associate clinical social workers and psychology assistants may render the above related psychology services under a supervising clinician. The claim must list the associate or assistant's name in the Additional Claim Information field (Box 19) or on an attachment, along with the supervising clinician's National Provider Identifier number as the "billing provider."' So an associate does not bill Medi-Cal in their own right and has no column; the supervising licensed clinician bills at the licensed-column rate and pays the associate whatever they pay them.
medicaid.structural_note: This is the finding that matters more than the number, and it undercuts the row's usefulness regardless of which column is quoted. The rate above is the fee-for-service schedule, and fee-for-service is now a residual delivery system in Medi-Cal. DHCS's own 'Medi-Cal at a Glance' (data month January 2025) reports 14,907,754 certified eligibles, of whom 14,040,781 (94.2%) are in managed care and 866,973 (5.8%) are fee-for-service. Mental health is then split two ways on top of that: non-specialty mental health services (NSMHS — the mild-to-moderate outpatient psychotherapy a solo private practitioner actually delivers) are the responsibility of the Medi-Cal managed care plan, per DHCS All Plan Letter 26-002 (issued February 2, 2026), which directs that 'MCPs must provide or arrange for the provision of the following NSMHS'; specialty mental health services for members meeting the SMHS access criteria in BHIN 26-002 run through county mental health plans, whose rates DHCS publishes separately at dhcs.ca.gov and which are explicitly plan-level rates — that page states the schedules 'contain rates that DHCS reimburses Mental Health Plans for services rendered to Medi-Cal beneficiaries', not rates paid to individual clinicians. The practical consequence: a solo LMFT in private practice who takes Medi-Cal is almost always contracted with a managed care plan or a county, and is paid a negotiated rate that is not published anywhere. The FFS schedule would only govern the ~5.8% FFS residual. So the honest answer is yes — this published rate is not the one that applies to most of this audience, and the row should say so rather than present any single number as 'what Medi-Cal pays'.

recommended_row.label: Medi-Cal fee-for-service, non-specialty mental health (90837)
recommended_row.associate: n/a — associates cannot bill; the supervising clinician is the billing provider
recommended_row.footnote: Medi-Cal Part 2 provider manual, 'Non-Specialty Mental Health Services: Reimbursement Rates and Billing Codes', psychotherapy table last updated December 2022. The schedule has two columns: 'MD, NP, PA' and 'LP, LCSW, LPCC, LMFT'. The $98.02 often quoted for 90837 is the physician column, not the therapist column. Two caveats. First, as published, 90837 (60 min, $38.01) pays less than 90834 (45 min, $67.16) in the therapist column — that is what the document says, and it looks like a defect in the document rather than policy, since $38.01 is also the published crisis-code rate in both columns. Second, and more important: this is the fee-for-service schedule, and only 5.8% of Medi-Cal is fee-for-service (DHCS, January 2025 data). Outpatient psychotherapy for the other 94.2% is a managed care plan responsibility (DHCS APL 26-002) or a county mental health plan responsibility, at negotiated rates that are not published. Treat this row as a floor reference, not as what a contracted Medi-Cal therapist is paid.

medicare.conversion_factor_note: CY2026 has TWO conversion factors for the first time, per CMS: $33.5675 for a Qualifying APM Participant (QP) and $33.4009 for a non-qualifying clinician. Both values were read directly out of the CONV FACTOR column of CMS's own RVU26A release files (PPRRVU2026_Jan_QPP.csv and PPRRVU2026_Jan_nonQPP.csv, released 12/29/2025), not from secondary reporting. $33.4009 is the correct one for a solo private-practice LMFT, who will essentially never be a QP in an Advanced APM. Using the QP factor instead raises every figure below by about 0.5% (e.g. Rest of California $130.16 instead of $129.52).
medicare.rvu_detail: CY2026 non-facility RVUs for 90837 ('Psytx w pt 60 minutes', status A): work 3.78, non-facility practice expense 1.20, malpractice 0.02, total non-facility 5.00. Source: CMS PPRRVU2026_Jan files. Cross-check: 5.00 x $33.4009 = $167.00, which matches the independently published 2026 national non-facility payment amount for 90837. For context on why the old number drifted, the CY2025 RVUs were work 3.63 / PE 1.06 / MP 0.08 at a $32.3465 conversion factor — 90837 got a substantial RVU increase for 2026 on top of the conversion-factor increase.
medicare.formula: Payment = [(work RVU x work GPCI) + (non-facility PE RVU x PE GPCI) + (MP RVU x MP GPCI)] x conversion factor. GPCIs are the FINAL CY2026 values from Addendum E (GPCI2026.csv in the RVU26A release). The LMFT amount is then 75% of that. All figures are ALLOWED amounts — Medicare pays 80% of the allowed amount and the beneficiary owes the other 20% as coinsurance, so the clinician collects the full figure shown, from two payers.

medicare.where_the_125_came_from: The existing ≈$125 is not fabricated — it is the CY2026 NATIONAL unadjusted figure ($125.25), with no geographic adjustment applied. Every California locality has GPCIs above 1.0 (practice-expense GPCI ranges from 1.096 in Rest of California to 1.442 in Santa Clara), so the California-correct figures run 3% to 19% higher than the national number. A second, weaker possibility is that it was the CY2025 Los Angeles figure, which computed to $123.81. Either way it is understated for California.
medicare.seventy_five_wording: The page's phrasing is correct and is in fact MORE precise than '75% of the PFS amount', so it should be kept. 42 U.S.C. §1395l(a)(1)(FF) pays marriage and family therapist and mental health counselor services at '80 percent of the lesser of the actual charge for the services or 75 percent of the amount determined for payment of a psychologist under subparagraph (L)'. Subparagraph (L), governing clinical psychologists, pays '80 percent of the lesser of the actual charge for the services or the amount determined by a fee schedule established by the Secretary' — i.e. the psychologist is paid the full physician fee schedule amount with no reduction. So the statute literally reduces to a percentage of the PSYCHOLOGIST amount, and because the psychologist amount equals the full PFS amount, '75% of the psychologist rate' and '75% of the PFS amount' resolve to the same number. Tracking the statute's own words is the better choice. Note the same 75% construction applies to clinical social workers under §1395l(a)(1)(F), so LMFT, LPCC and LCSW all land on the same figure. Note also that the '80 percent' in the statute is the Medicare share; the remaining 20% is beneficiary coinsurance, so the clinician still collects the full 75%-of-PFS allowed amount.
medicare.associate_finding: The current page's 'n/a' for the associate column is CORRECT and should be kept. 42 CFR §410.53(a) requires that to qualify, an MFT 'Is licensed or certified as a marriage and family therapist by the State in which the services are performed', possesses a qualifying master's or doctoral degree, and 'After obtaining such degree, has performed at least 2 years or 3,000 hours of post master's degree clinical supervised experience'. A pre-licensed AMFT/APCC/ASW therefore cannot enroll in or bill Medicare.

recommended_row.label: Medicare, CY2026 (90837) — LMFT / LCSW / LPCC at 75%
recommended_row.licensed: $130–$149 depending on locality (Rest of CA $129.52 · Los Angeles $134.47 · San Diego $133.75 · Sacramento $133.33 · San Francisco $146.29 · Santa Clara $148.66)
recommended_row.footnote: Computed from CMS's CY2026 published inputs, not quoted: total non-facility RVUs for 90837 of 5.00 (work 3.78, PE 1.20, MP 0.02), the CY2026 non-qualifying-APM conversion factor of $33.4009, and the final CY2026 California GPCIs from Addendum E — then reduced to 75% under 42 U.S.C. §1395l(a)(1)(FF), which pays MFT and mental health counselor services at '75 percent of the amount determined for payment of a psychologist'. Worked example, Rest of California: [3.78 × 1.017] + [1.20 × 1.096] + [0.02 × 0.536] = 5.17018 adjusted RVUs; × $33.4009 = $172.69 full physician fee schedule amount; × 0.75 = $129.52. These are allowed amounts — Medicare pays 80% and the client owes 20% coinsurance, so the practice collects the full figure from two sources. CY2026 is the first year with two conversion factors; $33.5675 applies to Qualifying APM Participants, which a solo private practice will not be, and would raise these figures by roughly 0.5%.

calvcb.effective: 12/15/2022, carried forward unchanged in the current revision whose third rate column is headed 'Rates Effective 6/1/2024'
calvcb.detail: Verified against the CalVCB Mental Health Provider Rates chart itself. The current chart (Rev. 5/2024) shows three rate columns — 4/1/2011, 12/15/2022 and 6/1/2024. Licensed Marriage Family Therapist (LMFT), Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) and Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor (LPCC) are each listed at $81/hour, then $105/hour, then $105/hour for individual/family therapy — so $105 took effect 12/15/2022 and was unchanged by the 6/1/2024 revision. Associate Marriage and Family Therapist (AMFT), Associate Clinical Social Worker (ASW) and Associate Professional Clinical Counselor (APCC), each 'must be supervised by a licensed therapist', are listed at $75, then $97, then $97/hour. Both $105 and $97 are confirmed. Worth knowing for context: these are individual/family therapy rates; group therapy is far lower ($32.40/hour licensed, $30/hour associate), a Licensed Psychologist gets $129/hour and a psychiatrist $152/hour. One housekeeping note — CalVCB's canonical link, victims.ca.gov/publications/mental-health-provider-rates-chart, still serves the older Rev. 11/2022 PDF, while the newer Rev. 5/2024 PDF lives at a different upload path. The two agree on $105/$97, so the figures hold either way; cite the 2024 file.

verdict: Both corrections hold, and both were confirmed from the primary documents rather than taken on trust — but they hold for different reasons and only one of them is a simple number swap.

Medicare is a clean fix: recompute from CMS's own CY2026 RVU release and the row is $129.52 (Rest of California) to $148.66 (Santa Clara), not ≈$125. I reproduced the research pass's figures to the cent, and independently validated the arithmetic against the published $167.00 national non-facility amount for 90837. The ≈$125 now on the page turns out to be the national unadjusted figure ($125.25) with no California GPCI applied — an understatement everywhere in the state. Keep the existing '75% of the psychologist rate' wording; 42 U.S.C. §1395l(a)(1)(FF) says exactly that, and it is more precise than '75% of the PFS amount', not less. Keep the 'n/a' in the associate column too — 42 CFR §410.53 requires full state licensure. High confidence.

Medi-Cal is NOT a simple number swap and should not be edited as one. The claim is correct on every factual point — the schedule really does have 'MD, NP, PA' and 'LP, LCSW, LPCC, LMFT' columns, $98.02 really is the physician column, the therapist column really does say $38.01 for 90837, and 90837 really does pay 43% less than 90834's $67.16 — but the $38.01 looks like a transcription defect in the DHCS document itself ($38.01 is the crisis-code rate published one row below in both columns), and, more decisively, only 5.8% of Medi-Cal is fee-for-service. Outpatient psychotherapy for the other 94.2% runs through managed care plans or county mental health plans at negotiated rates nobody publishes. Replacing $98 with $38.01 would trade one wrong number for a technically-correct one that is still not what this audience gets paid. The row should carry the licensed-column figures WITH the 90834 comparison and an explicit note that fee-for-service is a residual system — or be dropped from a table headed 'verifiable fee schedules'. The associate column must change regardless: $98 is wrong, associates have no Medi-Cal rate at all because the supervising clinician is the billing provider. High confidence on the facts, and the recommendation is deliberately to reframe the row rather than just renumber it.
CalVCB checks out unchanged: $105 licensed, $97 associate, effective 12/15/2022 and carried forward in the 6/1/2024 revision. No edit needed.
gaps: No published rate exists for what a Medi-Cal managed care plan or county mental health plan actually pays a contracted solo LMFT for 90837. MCP contracts are negotiated and not public, and the DHCS behavioral health fee schedules are plan-level rates DHCS pays the county, not clinician rates. This is the number the audience actually wants and it is genuinely unobtainable from public documents — worth saying so on the page.

I could not confirm whether Medi-Cal FFS actually ADJUDICATES 90837 at $38.01 for a licensed therapist, or whether the published table contains a transcription error that is corrected in the claims system. No DHCS erratum, provider bulletin, or correction was found. Resolving this would require a remittance advice from a clinician who has billed the code, or a direct query to DHCS/Medi-Cal provider relations. Until then the honest framing is 'this is what the published schedule says' rather than 'this is what you will be paid'.

The Medi-Cal psychotherapy rate table is stamped 'Page updated: December 2022'. It is definitely the live document (retrieved identical from two asset paths, and a sibling table in the same file was updated March 2025), but it predates recent Medi-Cal targeted provider rate increases, and I did not establish whether any of those increases touched NSMHS fee-for-service psychotherapy codes.

Medicare figures use the non-qualifying-APM conversion factor ($33.4009), which is right for a solo private practice. A clinician who is a Qualifying APM Participant would be paid at $33.5675, about 0.5% more. The page does not need to explain this, but the footnote should not claim a single universal figure without the caveat.

California has 29 Medicare payment localities. The row gives a range anchored on six; a clinician in Napa/Vallejo (PE GPCI 1.318) or Santa Rosa (1.228) falls between the endpoints and is not individually listed.

Medicare figures are the January 2026 release (RVU26A, released 12/29/2025). CMS issues quarterly corrections; a mid-year update could shift RVUs slightly. Re-check against the current-quarter RVU file before any future republication.
